knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 15-year-old female presented to the paediatrics outpatient department with progressive abnormal jerky body movements, difficulty walking, episodes of falling, and unusual behaviour over the past 18 months. There was no similar history in the family. The child had received all age-appropriate immunizations. Physical examination showed myoclonic jerks, increased muscle tone in all four limbs, reduced deep tendon reflexes, muscle strength of 5/5, and normal sensory system evaluation.. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 71-year-old male from Madrid, Spain, presented with a 2-month history of dysphonia. He has a 30-year history of smoking and underwent a liver transplant 8 years ago due to liver cirrhosis, currently on chronic immunosuppressant therapy with mycophenolate mofetil. The patient exhibited symptoms including dysphonia, dysphagia, odynophagia, autophony, fatigue, anorexia, and a weight loss of over 20 kg in the past 6 months. Fiber-optic laryngoscopy identified a vegetative lesion on the lingual surface of the epiglottis, extending to the epiglottic vallecula. A non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan showed increased soft tissue size on the lingual surface of the epiglottis.. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Histoplasmosis. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Histoplasmosis.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Subacute Histoplasmosis

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 36-year-old male presented with shortness of breath and swelling in the lower extremities for the past 2 weeks. The patient also reported experiencing intermittent fever over the last 2 months. Upon admission, vital signs included a heart rate of 103 beats per minute, blood pressure of 122/47 mmHg, and a temperature of 37.2°C. Cardiac examination identified a pandiastolic murmur in the aortic region. Laboratory tests indicated an elevated NT-proBNP level of 4492.0 pg/mL.. Confirmed diagnosis: Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis. Differential diagnosis includes: Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis.

knowledge_fragments.content: Cutaneous manifestations are frequent and often early features of both Kawasaki disease (KD) and multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C). Dermatologic findings are particularly relevant, as they may represent the first clinical clue and precede severe systemic complications.

tree.case_summary:
A 59-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for fatigue. In general, he has been in good health; however, he recently has experienced weight loss, abdominal pain, and general fatigue. He has a medical history of anxiety, diabetes, a fracture of his foot sustained when he tripped, and a recent cold that caused him to miss work for 1 week. His current medications include metformin, insulin, buspirone, vitamin D, calcium, and sodium docusate. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals a calm gentleman. A mild systolic murmur is heard in the left upper sternal region. The rest of the physical exam is within normal limits. Laboratory values are ordered as seen below. Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL Hematocrit: 36% Leukocyte count: 66,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 177,000/mm^3 Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase: elevated Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 120 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.9 mEq/L AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Acute lymphoblastic lymphoma
B. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
C. Chronic myeloid leukemia
D. Leukemoid reaction
E. Multiple myeloma
